angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 345,763 km at 143.71 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.9585 +/- 0.0236 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03): 143.71 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.497 +/- 0.013 solar radii from Premnath et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-7265 B b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...92P/abstract): 345,763 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.521 +/- 0.023 solar masses from Premnath et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-7265 B b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...92P/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3503 +/- 59 K from Premnath et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7265 B b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...92P/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Premnath et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7265 B b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...92P/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-7265-b.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.762, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
